title: Parallel sharded reranker with token-slice scheduling and KV-safety
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Problem: The reranking endpoint experiences high tail latency under mixed token-length workloads and high concurrency. Current continuous-batching and monolithic KV prefetch cause head-of-line blocking when a few long-token requests stall microbatches, and KV cache contention raises p99 under sustained load.

Goals:
- Reduce p95/p99 latency for typical multi-candidate rerank requests (avg candidate set sizes of 16–64) by at least 25% for 128–1024 token input ranges.
- Maintain or improve throughput and lower per-request token CPU/GPU cost by 10–15%.
- Preserve quality (no regression in rerank quality metrics: MRR and MAP on internal eval sets).
- Provide safe rollout with canarying and observability (per-shard latencies, KV read contention, microbatch sizes).

Proposed approach:
1) Sharded token-slice scheduler: split long inputs into fixed token slices (configurable, default 256) and schedule slices across lightweight lanes. Short requests remain on a fast lane to avoid serialization with long tails. Slices are reassembled post-score with order-preserving merge.
2) Opportunistic parallelization: when candidate scoring is independent (embeddings precomputed), allow parallel per-candidate scoring across lanes with a configurable parallelism cap to avoid OOM. This uses per-request token budget enforcement to limit worst-case slot usage.
3) KV-safety fence and prefetch window: introduce a per-shard KV prefetch fence that gates concurrent KV reads to a small window and prioritizes hottest keys. Add async prefetch on the fast lane for small inputs. This reduces hot-key contention under heavy traffic.
4) Soft deadlines and graceful degradation: implement soft timeouts per-slice that allow returning partial scores for straggling slices and flagging for re-score fallback to cheaper model if quality falls below threshold.
5) Runtime knobs + autosuggest: expose token-slice size, lane counts, per-request token budget, and parallelism cap; integrate into Optimize suggestions so customers get recommended defaults based on observed token distribution.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Complexity: slice reassembly and score consistency require careful ordering and testing; risk of subtle bugs in partial scoring.
- Quality: slicing could change model context dynamics and affect rerank scores; validation needed on internal eval sets and customer test prompts.
- Resource accounting: parallel per-candidate scoring increases peak memory; need strict per-request quotas and evictions to avoid cross-tenant impact.

Success metrics:
- p95 latency improvement >= 25% and p99 improvement >= 15% on benchmark harness for mixed token workloads.
- No >1% regression in rerank MRR on internal eval set.
- Reduction in CPU/GPU token cost >= 10% for rerank endpoint.

Rollout plan:
- Spike and benchmark (this ticket).
- Integration tests and cross-tenant chaos tests (simulate KV contention).
- Canary rollout on dedicated staging cluster (10% traffic) with traffic mirroring for quality checks.
- Gradual ramp with per-lane telemetry and auto-rollback if SLO regressions or quality drift detected.

Observability additions required: per-slice latency histograms, KV-prefetch hit/miss counters, per-request memory peak, partial-score rate, quality drift alerts tied to eval prompts.

Documentation and API: Add console toggles for token-slice mode and expose runtime metrics in Console and Optimize with recommended defaults.
comments: 2025-02-12 Priya Patel: Initial ticket filed after spike showed long-tail p99s on rerank under mixed workloads. Draft design attached (Confluence: /display/RNF/Parallel+Reranker+Token+Slice+Design).

2025-02-18 Liam Chen: Spike experiments complete. Early bench on A100 (64GB) shows p95 down 22% for mixed 16–128 candidate sets with slice=256, but p99 unchanged due to KV contention. Logged detailed traces: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/pull/3172
2025-02-20 Maya Ortega (SRE): Observed KV read queueing on high QPS. Suggested per-shard prefetch fence and limiting parallel prefetches to reduce tail. Added to design.

2025-02-26 Liam Chen: Implemented prototype of slice scheduler and per-request token budget enforcement. Unit tests added. Local integration shows partial-score fallback working. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/pull/3198

2025-03-01 Priya Patel (PM): Run evaluation on internal rerank eval harness (dataset rerank-dev-v2). No quality regression observed (MRR delta -0.2%). Need extended A/B with customer prompt subsets. Added to canary plan.

2025-03-04 Liam Chen: Bench update: with KV-safety fence and prefetch window, p99 improved by 18% and p95 by 30% on synthetic mixed workload. Preparing canary run configuration and dashboard widgets for per-slice telemetry. Planning canary for 2025-03-15.
